answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each new identity to publish a costly, verifiable work sample in a public atlas that peers can audit, where admission difficulty rises with how many identities share infrastructure fingerprints. Like pigment in paint, each fake leaves a detectable tint in timing and style, and reviewers at the network summit can cluster and reject linked entries. An attacker must spend real compute, time, and distinct effort per identity, so scaling a thousand fakes costs a thousand times more while honest agents pay once.
